question: Which of the following is NOT a safe home modification for preventing mobility-related falls?

options.A: Ensuring bright and steady lighting along hallway floors
options.B: Placing loose decorative throw rugs over slippery tile floors
options.C: Installing grab bars securely next to the toilet and shower
options.D: Clearing electrical cords completely out of walking pathways

explanation: Loose throw rugs slide easily under feet or assistive devices, making them a major hazard for causing patient falls. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h6)

question: What does 'psychological safety' mean for a quality improvement team?

options.A: Members feel safe speaking up without fear of punishment
options.B: All physical meeting rooms have secure electronic locks
options.C: Patient medical records remain strictly confidential
options.D: Staff members never experience physical fatigue at work

explanation: Exactly! When a team has psychological safety, staff feel comfortable sharing honest feedback and reporting mistakes without fear of being mocked or punished.

question: Which psychological condition is often seen in women and girls who have survived FGM?

options.A: Bipolar manic depression with hallucinations
options.B: Obsessive compulsive cleaning disorder
options.C: Post-traumatic stress disorder and anxiety
options.D: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder

explanation: Spot on! The painful and terrifying experience often leaves survivors with long-term emotional trauma, anxiety, and distress.

question: Which of these is a foundational lifestyle change for managing hypertension?

options.A: Adopting a healthy diet low in sodium and exercising regularly
options.B: Increasing daily fluid intake with high-sugar beverages
options.C: Taking daily high-dose over-the-counter anti-inflammatory drugs
options.D: Avoiding all physical activity to keep the heart rate very low

explanation: Lifestyle is medicine! Eating less salt, staying active, and managing weight are the best first steps to keep blood pressure in check.

question: What makes ethical choices so emotionally heavy for nurses during a major disaster?

options.A: Having to ration scarce life-saving resources among many needy patients
options.B: Having too many modern medical machines to choose from
options.C: Working in fully air-conditioned and quiet field offices
options.D: Patients having unlimited time to discuss treatment options

explanation: So true. Deciding who gets scarce life-saving care when there isn't enough to go around is one of the hardest emotional burdens a nurse can carry.

question: What does the clinical communication shortcut SBAR stand for?

options.A: Safety, Background, Analysis, Report
options.B: System, Barrier, Assessment, Recovery
options.C: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.D: Symptoms, Behavior, Action, Response

explanation: SBAR is your best friend during handovers and doctor calls! It keeps your communication clear, quick, and structured.

question: Why do the bulbourethral glands release a clear mucus right before ejaculation?

options.A: To neutralize any leftover acid from urine in the urethra
options.B: To provide the main energy source for sperm motility
options.C: To activate sperm flagella for faster swimming
options.D: To cause the semen to clot firmly inside the vagina

explanation: Urine is quite acidic and can harm delicate sperm. This clever little mucus fluid cleanses the urethra path first so the sperm can pass safely!

question: Why are broad-spectrum antibiotics started immediately instead of waiting for lab results?

options.A: Culture results are always inaccurate during the postpartum period
options.B: Delaying treatment allows the infection to worsen rapidly and threaten life
options.C: Broad-spectrum drugs have no side effects for the nursing mother
options.D: Hospital accreditation standards fine units that delay medication

explanation: Sepsis is a race against time! Waiting days for lab results could let the infection spiral out of control, so we start treatment right away.

question: Which clinical sign tells you that an antibiotic is successfully beating the infection?

options.A: Elevation in patient blood pressure readings
options.B: Complete disappearance of normal skin flora
options.C: Increase in patient appetite within one hour
options.D: Reduction in fever and white blood cell count

explanation: Brilliant! Watching the fever drop and WBC count return to normal is a classic nursing win.

question: Why is blood typing and crossmatching ordered right away for a patient with heavy post-abortion bleeding?

options.A: To check for chronic viral infections
options.B: To figure out how many weeks pregnant she was
options.C: To have matching blood ready for an emergency transfusion
options.D: To find out if she is allergic to IV fluids

explanation: Heavy bleeding drops blood volume fast, so having matched blood on standby is a lifesaver. You're thinking like a true nurse!

question: Why are open-ended questions best when taking a drug history?

options.A: They are much faster to document in the nursing notes
options.B: They stop the patient from talking too much
options.C: They encourage the patient to share detailed, honest information
options.D: They prevent the patient from asking about their hospital bill

explanation: Open-ended questions let patients explain their routines in their own words instead of just saying yes or no. Excellent interviewing tip for the wards!

question: In which position should you place a patient who is having an upper gastrointestinal endoscopy?

options.A: High Fowler sitting upright
options.B: Supine flat on the back
options.C: Left lateral position
options.D: Prone face down on the bed

explanation: Lying on the left side is safest—it keeps the airway open and lets any saliva drain out easily without choking them.

question: What is the primary role of a critical care nurse during patient assessment?

options.A: Prescribing emergency medications independently
options.B: Performing surgical interventions at the bedside
options.C: Replacing laboratory diagnostic equipment
options.D: Detecting subtle physiological changes early

explanation: The critical care nurse serves as a continuous observer to catch small warning signs before a patient deteriorates fully. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T2#GNS321_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which mental health challenge is commonly seen in teenage mothers after childbirth?

options.A: Postpartum depression
options.B: Schizophrenic psychosis
options.C: Bipolar manic disorder
options.D: Obsessive-compulsive hoarding

explanation: The sudden shift to parenting, lack of emotional maturity, and feeling alone place teenage mothers at high risk for postpartum depression.

question: Why is it important to involve traditional and religious leaders in health mobilisation?

options.A: They hold strong moral authority and influence public opinion
options.B: They write the national nursing curriculum
options.C: They are the only people who understand modern medicine
options.D: They are required by law to fund all local pharmacies

question: Which group of nutrients does the body need in large amounts?

options.A: Macronutrients
options.B: Micronutrients
options.C: Trace elements
options.D: Antioxidants

explanation: Macro means large! Macronutrients like carbs, proteins, and fats are the big-ticket items our bodies need in heavy quantities every day.

question: What happens when food moves way too quickly through a person's colon?

options.A: Ulceration
options.B: Appendicitis
options.C: Diarrhea
options.D: Constipation

explanation: If food rushes through the colon, there's no time to absorb water, leading to loose, watery stools. Makes total sense when you picture it!

question: A community health nurse finds three new cases of tuberculosis in a neighborhood. What is the best immediate step for managing the human reservoir?

options.A: Spraying chemical disinfectants on local streets and pathways
options.B: Tracing and screening close contacts of the infected individuals
options.C: Ordering all residents in the town to stay indoors for a month
options.D: Vaccinating all stray dogs and cats living near the neighborhood

explanation: Contact tracing lets us find other people who might be carrying the germ without knowing it yet, so they can get checked and treated early.

question: When is medication reconciliation most critical for a patient?

options.A: During every routine morning bath
options.B: Only when the patient is discharged home
options.C: During transitions of care between settings
options.D: Right before a surgical incision is closed

explanation: Medication reconciliation is vital whenever a patient moves between different healthcare settings or levels of care, as this is when errors happen most. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T2#GNS215_U2_T2_h2)

question: In clinical practice, what do healthcare standards actually give us?

options.A: A formula for calculating hospital budgets
options.B: A list of punishments for clinical errors
options.C: A yardstick for measuring safe and competent performance
options.D: A strict schedule for nurse shift rotations

explanation: Spot on! Standards act as our baseline guide or 'yardstick' to make sure our nursing care is always safe, skilled, and professional.

question: Which nerve is most vulnerable to being stretched or compressed during a tough vaginal delivery?

options.A: Sciatic nerve
options.B: Pudendal nerve
options.C: Femoral nerve
options.D: Vagus nerve

question: Why is it important to complete admission documentation promptly rather than waiting until the end of a long shift?

options.A: So that nurses can leave work before their shift officially ends
options.B: To allow the patient to take the paper home immediately
options.C: Because ward managers check handwriting speeds daily
options.D: To prevent forgetting important clinical details and ensure safety

explanation: Writing down observations immediately ensures accuracy and provides oncoming staff with up-to-date information for safe care delivery. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is manually copying patient data dangerous in a clinical setting?

options.A: It automatically deletes vital sign history from the computer
options.B: It prevents the pharmacy from ever dispensing any drugs
options.C: It causes the hospital internet network to crash completely
options.D: It increases the risk of transcription errors and delays

explanation: Spotting mistakes is key to safe nursing! Copying things by hand takes extra time and opens the door to human errors that could affect patient safety. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why should you connect a health topic to the daily life experiences of adult learners?

options.A: Ministry regulations state that lectures must last for at least two hours

options.C: Older individuals cannot memorize new information without a story
options.D: Adults learn best when the topic directly relates to their current life challenges

explanation: Exactly! When learners see how a topic solves their everyday problems, their motivation and memory skyrocket.

question: A hospital ward has a broken fan, uncomfortable chairs, and delayed salaries, making the nurses very upset. What do these represent in Herzberg's theory?

options.A: Hygiene factors causing job dissatisfaction
options.B: Self-actualization blocks in Maslow's pyramid
options.C: Motivators driving professional growth
options.D: Intrinsic rewards missing from daily tasks

explanation: When basic things like pay and a comfortable environment are messed up, workers get frustrated right away—no matter how much they love nursing!

question: What type of tissue lines the part of the urethra closest to the bladder?

options.A: Ciliated simple columnar epithelium
options.B: Stratified cuboidal epithelium
options.C: Simple squamous epithelium
options.D: Transitional epithelium

question: What is the best immediate response when a colleague reacts with anger to your assertive concern?

options.A: Agree immediately that you were wrong
options.B: Shout back so they know you are serious
options.C: Walk away and never report the safety issue
options.D: Stay calm and keep the focus on clinical facts

explanation: Keeping your emotions in check and focusing on patient safety prevents the conflict from getting worse. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h7)

question: What three areas does the famous Donabedian model look at to measure healthcare quality?

options.A: Structure, process, and outcome
options.B: Assessment, planning, and evaluation
options.C: Admission, treatment, and discharge
options.D: Staffing, funding, and equipment

question: Why is growing different types of crops (crop diversity) on small farms good for community nutrition?

options.A: It stops pests from destroying the main staple crop
options.B: It prevents seasonal vitamin deficiencies by providing varied nutrients
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for agricultural irrigation

question: A young student in Nigeria worries that taking Postinor-2 will make her barren. How should you respond?

options.A: Prescribe a strong surgical procedure to clear her reproductive system
options.B: Scold her for engaging in premarital sex and refuse to give her the medication

question: Why is preparing a patient for common drug side effects an important counselling objective?

options.A: It guarantees that the disease will never return again
options.B: It allows the patient to sell extra doses to others safely
options.C: It prevents patients from panicking and stopping treatment early
options.D: It eliminates all biological reactions to the medication

explanation: When patients know what mild side effects to expect, they are less likely to abandon their prescription out of fear. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h1)

question: What is the first emergency medicine to give if a newborn's heart rate stays under 60 despite breathing support and chest compressions?

options.A: Naloxone
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Sodium bicarbonate
options.D: Epinephrine

question: Why do public health institutions need to be accountable in multiple directions?

options.A: To allow private individuals to take over hospital ownership
options.B: To ensure proper use of public funds and maintain clinical standards
options.C: To remove the need for any government budget allocation
options.D: To make sure doctors outrank nurses in every administrative decision

explanation: Exactly! Because these institutions handle public money and human lives, we must check both financial honesty and top-notch clinical care.

question: How does spacing children properly help a mother's health?

options.A: It guarantees an easier delivery without any pain management
options.B: It lowers the risks of pregnancy complications and maternal death
options.C: It speeds up the physical aging process of reproductive organs
options.D: It permanently eliminates all future risks of chronic illness

question: What is the main purpose of tracheobronchial suctioning?

options.A: Removing secretions to keep the airway clear

question: In ward inventory, what does hitting your 'minimum stock level' tell you?

options.A: It is the exact number of items used in a single day

options.C: It is the maximum amount the store can hold

question: What is the main use of short-acting beta-agonists (SABAs) in asthma care?

question: Why is family caregiver education especially important when nursing pediatric special needs patients at home?

options.A: Children do not require any medical monitoring once discharged

question: Which portable device does a patient wear to continuously send heart rhythm data to the nurse's station?

question: What is papilledema?

question: Why might a nurse rush to handle a sudden disease outbreak over a common chronic illness?

options.A: The high severity and community panic demand immediate action

question: Why must a nurse demonstrate the call bell system immediately upon a patient's arrival?

options.A: It distracts the patient from their current physical pain
options.B: It gives the patient a direct way to call for help when needed
options.C: It proves to the visiting family members that the equipment works
options.D: Hospital policy requires it to be tested every single hour

question: Why is an elevated pulse often considered an early warning sign of patient distress?

question: What does standard deviation mainly tell us about a set of healthcare data?

question: What type of medicine is often given to hospitalized COVID-19 patients to prevent blood clots?

options.D: Antibiotics

question: When should physical or chemical restraints be used during a behavioral crisis?

options.A: Whenever the nursing staff feels mildly inconvenienced

options.D: Only when ordered by a family member

question: What usually happens during data analysis if a research study completely lacks a theoretical framework?

question: What is the main job of a research question in a nursing study?

question: A nurse notices a sudden rise in wound infections on the surgical ward. What makes surveillance data valuable here?

question: What is the primary function of vitamins and minerals in our metabolism?

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating a newly introduced nursing practice?

question: Why do some communities continue to practice FGM across generations?

question: What is the primary goal of a physiotherapist working with an older adult?

question: Why is setting up a large IV line so important for an anaemic woman in labor?

question: Why do many families continue traditional practices that might be harmful to health?

question: Which of these is a classic example of a Clinical Decision Support System in action?

question: What is the main reason for keeping vaccines in the cold chain?

question: Why should a nurse avoid using heavy Mayo scissors to cut fine sutures or delicate tissue?

question: What happens to the baby's blood pressure right after the umbilical cord is clamped?

options.C: Four family member approvals

explanation: Using identifiers like the patient's name and hospital number ensures the right person receives the treatment. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h3)

question: What delayed complication of a sting can show up days later with fever, joint pain, and a skin rash?

options.A: Hyperglycemia
options.B: Serum sickness
options.C: Cellulitis
options.D: Anaphylactic shock

explanation: Correct! Serum sickness is an immune system reaction that can pop up several days after exposure, causing fever, aching joints, and rashes.

question: Why do nurses write and share research reports?

options.A: To criticize current hospital management policies
options.B: To fulfill a graduation requirement without clinical use
options.C: To promote personal medical opinions to the public
options.D: To communicate new knowledge for evidence-based practice

explanation: You got this! Research turns everyday clinical questions into clear evidence we can use to give our patients the best care possible.

question: Which group of people faces a much higher risk of experiencing interpersonal violence?

options.A: Retired corporate executives
options.B: Middle-aged professional athletes
options.C: Pregnant women and young children
options.D: Healthy young adult males living by themselves

explanation: You got it! Vulnerable groups like pregnant women, children, and older adults statistically experience higher rates of abuse and neglect.

question: As a student nurse, what should be your main focus when giving nutrition advice to a patient?

options.A: Diagnosing eating disorders
options.B: Helping patients make healthy food choices
options.C: Calculating daily calorie intake
options.D: Prescribing strict medical diets

explanation: Great job thinking like a nurse! Nutrition counselling isn't about rigid rules; it's about guiding people toward healthy, sustainable food decisions that fit their everyday lives.

question: Why is clear, informed consent so important before a couple starts IVF treatment?

options.A: Because nurses are legally required to adopt any resulting children
options.B: Because it prevents patients from ever experiencing natural conception again
options.C: Because decisions must be made early about storing or donating leftover embryos
options.D: Because IVF is completely illegal under all Nigerian federal statutes

explanation: Since IVF creates extra embryos, couples must agree in advance on what will happen to them to avoid future legal and emotional conflicts. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h6)

question: What is an autoantigen?

options.A: A synthetic chemical manufactured inside a sterile laboratory
options.B: A protein transferred from an animal graft to a human patient
options.C: A normal body tissue mistakenly attacked by the immune system
options.D: A harmful bacterial toxin inhaled directly from the outside air

explanation: 'Auto' means self. An autoantigen happens when the immune system gets confused and mistakenly treats normal body parts like enemies.

question: What is one of the key roles of a nurse when acting as a facilitator in community mobilisation?

options.A: Writing laws that fine people who refuse to visit the clinic
options.B: Helping local committees run meetings and prioritize health problems
options.C: Taking over all financial accounts of the local government
options.D: Purchasing private cars for all members of the village council

explanation: As facilitators, nurses guide the process without dominating it, helping residents make their own decisions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h5)

question: What is the most effective way at the community level to stop the spread of paragonimiasis?

options.A: Treating entire river water sources with heavy industrial chlorine
options.B: Banning the commercial sale of all freshwater fish species
options.C: Immunizing all school-aged children with a parasite vaccine
options.D: Educating the public to cook freshwater crabs thoroughly

explanation: Spot on! Health education is key. Teaching people to cook their crabs thoroughly stops the parasite right in its tracks.

question: Why is a chest X-ray routinely ordered after a thoracocentesis?

options.A: To check if any skin sutures need to be removed immediately
options.B: To confirm lung re-expansion and rule out a pneumothorax
options.C: To measure the exact weight of the remaining heart tissue
options.D: To prove that the patient has completely recovered from the flu

explanation: A post-procedure chest X-ray helps verify that the lung expanded properly and that no air leaked into the pleural space during the procedure. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h6)

question: What unit of measurement do electronic IV infusion pumps typically use to set fluid rates?

options.A: Liters per 24 hours
options.B: Milliliters per hour
options.C: Drops per second
options.D: Grams per minute

explanation: Infusion pumps are programmed directly in mL/hr to deliver precise fluid volumes over time. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h7)

question: What is the very first thing you should do for a baby right after a home birth?

options.A: Transport the newborn immediately to a distant clinic
options.B: Give the baby a full soap bath in warm water
options.C: Dry the infant thoroughly with a clean, warm towel
options.D: Clamp and cut the umbilical cord before drying

explanation: Drying and wrapping the baby fast is key to keeping them warm and preventing cold stress.

question: What is the classic early symptom of Spinal Cord Compression in cancer patients?

options.A: Inability to swallow
options.B: New, persistent back pain
options.C: Sudden visual loss
options.D: Severe chest pain

explanation: Back pain that worsens when lying flat is almost always the earliest warning sign of a tumor pressing on the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h3)

question: As a midwife checking the lower boundary of the pelvic cavity, which bones help form the pelvic outlet?

options.A: Acetabulum and pubic tubercle
options.B: Ischial tuberosities and coccyx
options.C: Linea terminalis and sacral ala
options.D: Iliac crests and sacral promontory

explanation: Think of the bottom exit of the pelvis: it's bounded by your tailbone (coccyx), the sitting bones (ischial tuberosities), and the front pubic bone.

question: What are the prominent parallel ridges found on the front surface of the medulla called?

options.A: The pyramids
options.B: The olives
options.C: The pons
options.D: The peduncles

explanation: You got it! The pyramids are the distinct ridges on the front (anterior) surface of the medulla that carry important motor pathways down from the brain. Keep building that knowledge!

question: A patient asks why a food with a high glycemic index can sometimes still be eaten in small amounts. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: The glycemic index only applies to people who do not take insulin.
options.B: Glycemic load looks at actual portion size, so a small serving has less overall impact.
options.C: Small amounts of high GI foods completely cure insulin resistance.
options.D: High GI foods automatically turn into low GI foods if you chew them slowly.

explanation: Glycemic load combines the GI score with the actual amount of food eaten, giving a realistic picture of blood sugar impact. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h3)

question: How do the results of an MBO performance review affect the future?

options.A: They feed directly into the planning cycle for the next period
options.B: They replace the need for patient care audits
options.C: They are permanently locked away and never looked at again
options.D: They are used to reduce the hospital training budget

explanation: Lessons learned from evaluating past performance help shape better, more realistic goals for the next MBO cycle. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h7)

question: What do home ovulation predictor kits mainly test for in urine?

options.A: Human chorionic gonadotropin
options.B: Luteinizing hormone
options.C: Basal body temperature
options.D: Estrogen metabolites only

explanation: Ovulation kits look for that telltale surge of luteinizing hormone in the urine, which usually happens a day or two before ovulation.

question: What is the main reason for 'physiological haemodilution' in pregnant women?

options.A: The bone marrow fails to produce any new blood cells
options.B: Red blood cells are actively destroyed by the maternal immune system
options.C: Plasma volume increases much more than red blood cell mass
options.D: Iron absorption in the small intestine drops to zero

explanation: Think of it like adding more water to juice—the fluid volume increases much faster than the red blood cells, making the blood appear 'thinned out' on lab tests. Completely normal and expected in pregnancy!

question: Which blood lab results would you expect to see if a patient's kidneys are suddenly failing?

options.A: Zero detectable sodium ions in blood plasma
options.B: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
options.C: Lowered levels of circulating metabolic waste products
options.D: High concentrations of plasma red blood cells

explanation: Spot on! When the kidneys aren't filtering well, waste products like creatinine and urea build up quickly in the blood.

question: You check a patient's blood pressure and find it dangerously high while they complain of severe chest pain. What do you do right away?

options.A: Erase the reading and take it again tomorrow
options.B: Wait until the shift handover meeting later that evening
options.C: Leave the patient room without telling anyone
options.D: Report the critical findings verbally to the physician immediately

explanation: Critical changes need fast action! Always speak up and report urgent findings right away to senior staff or the doctor so the patient gets help immediately.

question: What does emotional health really mean for a person?

options.A: Having a high intelligence quotient
options.B: A dynamic state of coping with life and realizing one's potential
options.C: The total absence of any stressful life events
options.D: Always feeling happy and joyful throughout the day

explanation: Emotional health isn't about being happy 24/7 or having zero stress. It's about balance, bouncing back from normal life challenges, and functioning well!

question: Parenteral nutrition delivers concentrated calories and nutrients directly into which part of the body?

options.A: The muscular tissue of the upper thigh
options.B: The bloodstream through a central venous catheter
options.C: The stomach cavity through a percutaneous tube
options.D: The small intestine through a nasal tube

explanation: Parenteral nutrition bypasses the gut completely and sends nutrients straight into the bloodstream via a central line.

question: How should numbers inside a research table column normally be aligned?

options.A: To the right or by decimal points
options.B: Centered with uneven spacing
options.C: To the extreme left margin
options.D: Diagonally across the cells

explanation: Right-aligning or lining up numbers by their decimal points makes it super easy to compare sizes up and down at a glance.

question: Why is it so important to chew your food thoroughly before swallowing?

options.A: To activate salivary lipase completely inside the mouth
options.B: To increase the surface area of food for better enzyme action
options.C: To remove all bacteria before the food enters the esophagus
options.D: To change the chemical pH of the food from acidic to basic

explanation: Chewing breaks big chunks of food into tiny pieces. This gives digestive enzymes a much larger surface area to work on, making digestion way more efficient!

question: A nurse is feeling burnt out after seeing multiple emergency cases. Which type of support is best?

options.A: Formative supervision
options.B: Restorative supervision
options.C: Administrative supervision
options.D: Normative supervision

explanation: When clinical work drains you emotionally, restorative supervision steps in to restore your peace of mind and help you cope with stress.

question: What is the main goal of descriptive statistics in a study?

options.A: Summarize the basic features and scores of the sample data
options.B: Replace the need for taking patient medical histories
options.C: Prove that a new drug cures a disease in all humans
options.D: Determine the financial cost of running a hospital ward

explanation: Descriptive statistics give you a quick, clear snapshot of what your sample looks like using simple summaries like averages and percentages.

question: Which specific Nigerian law is dedicated to protecting the rights and welfare of children?

options.A: The Public Health Safety Code
options.B: The Child Rights Act
options.C: The National Minimum Wage Act
options.D: The Land Use Decree

explanation: Keep this one handy! The Child Rights Act is the key legal backing we use to protect Nigerian children against abuse, exploitation, and early marriage.

question: What is the main difference between constructive and destructive conflict in a healthcare team?

options.A: Constructive conflict only happens in hospitals, while destructive conflict happens in clinics
options.B: Constructive conflict involves physical fighting, while destructive conflict involves silence
options.C: Constructive conflict improves patient care ideas, while destructive conflict harms team morale
options.D: Constructive conflict is ignored by managers, while destructive conflict is punished

explanation: Healthy disagreement challenges ideas for the better, whereas destructive conflict attacks personalities and breaks down teamwork. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h5)

question: Which group is generally most at risk for malnutrition and vaccine-preventable infections?

options.A: Retired civil servants receiving regular pensions
options.B: University students living in private hostels
options.C: Employed adult males aged thirty to forty
options.D: Children under five years of age

explanation: Under-fives are still building their immune systems and need plenty of nutrients, making them the most vulnerable group.

question: Why do researchers use statistical tables alongside written text in a report?

options.A: Narrative text cannot contain numbers under any circumstance
options.B: Tables summarize precise values so the text can focus on main findings
options.C: Tables are meant to confuse readers who do not understand math
options.D: Tables are required by law for every medical document

explanation: Tables make heavy numbers easy to look at, which lets the written text focus on the most important patient care takeaways without getting cluttered.

question: Which of these is a classic side effect of anticholinergic drugs all over the body?

options.A: Excessive sweating
options.B: Diarrhea
options.C: Dry mouth
options.D: Low heart rate

explanation: Since these drugs dry up body secretions, a very thirsty, dry mouth is the classic side effect patients always complain about!

question: What sign tells you a patient is struggling and working extra hard to breathe?

options.A: Warm and dry skin on the forehead
options.B: Use of accessory neck and chest muscles
options.C: Symmetrical and slow chest wall rise
options.D: Quiet and relaxed abdominal movement

explanation: When breathing gets tough, the neck and shoulder muscles kick in to help pull air in. Watch those shoulders!

question: What should an instructor do if students keep struggling to understand a concept after a lesson?

options.A: Blame the students for lacking basic intelligence
options.B: Ignore the failure and move on to the next chapter
options.C: Remove all practical work from the nursing curriculum
options.D: Revise the activity or adjust the teaching method

explanation: If a topic is tough to grasp, a good educator changes the approach so everyone can succeed. Learning is a two-way street!

question: If you hear fine crackling sounds in a patient's lower lung fields using your stethoscope, what does that usually mean?

options.A: Complete obstruction of the trachea
options.B: Fluid accumulation in the alveoli
options.C: Enlargement of the primary bronchi
options.D: Severe spasm of the vocal cords

question: At what age does the posterior fontanelle usually close up?

options.A: By the end of the second year
options.B: 2 to 3 months of age
options.C: At birth
options.D: 9 to 18 months of age

explanation: Correct! Because it's the smaller one, the posterior fontanelle closes early, usually by 2 to 3 months.

question: A patient comes in with a high fever and body aches. What important detail should you ask about first?

options.A: Recent travel and possible mosquito bites
options.B: Their family heart disease history
options.C: When they last visited the dentist
options.D: What vitamins they take daily

explanation: Spot on! Always check for local vector exposures like mosquitoes when dealing with fevers in our environment.

question: A nurse notices a resident's food intake has dropped sharply over two weeks. What is the best next step?

options.A: Collaborate with the interprofessional team to update the care plan
options.B: Wait for the annual assessment to record the weight loss
options.C: Discharge the resident to an assisted living facility
options.D: Stop monitoring meal intake since preferences change

question: Why do nurses convert raw tally numbers into percentages and rates when analyzing data?

options.A: To make the final report look more complicated to read
options.B: To eliminate the need to collect any information from households
options.C: To make the health findings easier to interpret and compare
options.D: To prevent community members from understanding the results

explanation: Spot on! Percentages and rates give meaning to raw numbers, helping us clearly see the proportion of people affected by an issue.

question: How does the hypothalamus talk directly to the anterior pituitary gland?

options.A: By sending electrical nerve impulses across a large fluid gap
options.B: Through direct nerve connections without any chemical messengers
options.C: By shedding cellular tissue directly into the cerebrospinal fluid
options.D: Through a specialized system of blood vessels called the portal system

question: How does it affect disaster response when agencies work in isolated 'silos'?

options.A: They eliminate all forms of bureaucratic delay within government offices
options.B: They automatically improve the speed of patient care at hospital bedsides
options.C: They protect their own budgets and authority instead of sharing resources

explanation: When groups work in isolation, they hoard supplies and info instead of sharing, which weakens the whole emergency response.

question: What is the main reason we dry a newborn baby off immediately after birth?

options.A: To remove residual vernix caseosa
options.B: To assess for congenital skin defects
options.C: To stimulate the cardiovascular system
options.D: To prevent heat loss through evaporation

question: How do compulsions usually help a patient dealing with this condition?

options.A: They are physical exercises prescribed to improve general body tone
options.B: They serve as temporary relief from the anxiety caused by obsessions
options.C: They are creative hobbies used to express hidden artistic talents
options.D: They help the patient hallucinate pleasant images to pass the time

explanation: You got it! Compulsions are the repeated actions patients feel forced to do just to calm down the heavy anxiety sparked by their obsessions.

question: Why do patients with upper motor neuron injuries often develop tight, spastic muscles over time?

options.A: Loss of normal inhibitory control from higher brain centers
options.B: Permanent blockage of blood flow to the spinal nerves
options.C: Severe inflammation within the peripheral nerve endings
options.D: Direct destruction of the skeletal muscle fibers in the limbs

question: Why are basic averages and percentages not enough on their own for explanatory research?

options.A: They can only be calculated by certified medical doctors
options.B: They are completely illegal to use in modern nursing journals
options.C: They do not prove whether one variable directly caused a change in another

explanation: Brilliant! Averages only describe numbers, but explanatory research needs deeper tests to prove cause and effect.

question: How does the 'collaborating' style work in the Thomas-Kilmann model?

options.A: It gives up complete control just to keep the peace on the ward.

options.C: It uses low assertiveness and low cooperativeness to ignore the problem entirely.

explanation: Collaboration is all about working together closely so both sides feel fully heard and completely satisfied with the result.

question: What condition involves widespread, abnormal blood clotting followed by severe bleeding due to used-up clotting factors?

options.A: Chronic venous insufficiency
options.B: Pulmonary hypertension
options.C: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
options.D: Acute respiratory distress syndrome

question: What happens when you wash your hands and stop a germ from reaching a patient?

options.A: The reservoir completely disappears

options.C: A link in the chain of infection is broken
options.D: The patient becomes immune to all diseases

question: What is a major systemic challenge frequently facing primary health care centers in Nigeria today?

options.B: Excessive supplies of clean water and electricity

question: What physical sign on a skin boil strongly points to a live, breathing larva hidden underneath?

question: What is the main job of salivary amylase in your mouth?

options.A: Breaking down complex starches into simpler sugars
options.B: Dissolving dietary proteins into basic amino acids
options.C: Destroying harmful bacteria found in drinking water
options.D: Lubricating the esophagus to prevent tearing

question: What is the main goal of spermatogenesis in the male body?

options.A: Maturation of mature oocytes
options.B: Secretion of seminal fluid proteins
options.C: Production of haploid spermatozoa
options.D: Formation of diploid spermatogonia

explanation: Think of spermatogenesis as the factory process that turns immature germ cells into mature sperm cells with half the normal chromosomes, ready for fertilization!

question: Why must used needles and medical waste be disposed of with extreme care in a disaster camp?

options.A: To provide building materials for temporary shelters
options.B: To make the garbage bags look neat and tidy
options.C: To keep the air smelling fresh for the residents
options.D: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries and biological contamination

explanation: Throwing sharps around carelessly can easily injure children playing nearby or fellow health workers. Safety first, always!

question: Why do we strictly control the movement of people inside a surgical suite?

options.A: To ensure the nurses finish their paperwork on time
options.B: To make sure doctors do not get lost in the hospital
options.C: To keep the surgical equipment from being stolen
options.D: To prevent the spread of microorganisms into sterile areas

question: By which physical mechanism do oxygen and carbon dioxide cross the placental membrane?

options.A: Pinocytosis

question: A 10-year-old child frequently misses school to nurse an ailing parent because other relatives live far away. What is happening here?

options.A: Unusually high community social participation

options.C: Role overload and premature parentification
options.D: Perfect balance of domestic responsibilities

explanation: When kids have to take on adult nursing duties due to lack of support, it leads to role overload and missed education.

question: A survivor of forced marriage discloses her situation to a nurse in confidence. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Post the details of the case on social media to raise quick awareness
options.B: Advise the patient to return home and obey her spouse to keep the peace
options.C: Maintain confidentiality while safely connecting her with social services and support
options.D: Inform the village elders immediately to resolve the family dispute

question: Which method is commonly used to find out about past exposures in a case-control study?

options.A: Surgical intervention
options.B: Randomized clinical trials
options.C: Direct laboratory observation of future events
options.D: Interviews and questionnaires

question: Which of these is an example of an Instrumental Activity of Daily Living (IADL)?

options.D: Bathing

question: Which tool do doctors commonly use to look inside the uterus and remove small fibroids?

options.D: Hysteroscope

question: What is the main goal of health economics?

options.A: Maximizing profit margins for pharmaceutical manufacturers
options.B: Eliminating all out-of-pocket expenses for hospital patients
options.C: Allocating scarce medical resources to meet healthcare needs
options.D: Regulating the number of medical schools in the country

question: A community nurse partners with local farmers and school headmasters to combat child malnutrition. Which concept does this action best demonstrate?

options.A: Private health insurance
options.B: Intersectoral linkages

options.D: Acute hospital management

question: Why do nurses do an evaluation stage at the end of a counselling process?

options.A: To collect payment for the session
options.B: To review the progress made toward set goals
options.C: To extend the therapy sessions indefinitely
options.D: To punish the patient for not following advice

explanation: Evaluating lets you and your patient look back and celebrate how far they've come toward their goals!

question: Why might a country with a growing economy still have poor public health funding?

options.A: Private citizens refuse to use public healthcare facilities

options.C: Economic growth automatically decreases the total population size
options.D: Government policy priorities may direct funds away from the health sector

question: Which major medical breakthrough in the 1950s helped patients leave large asylums for community care?

options.A: The introduction of early psychotropic medications

options.C: The invention of the modern stethoscope
options.D: The creation of structured group psychotherapy

question: What is considered the single most effective measure to prevent the spread of germs?

options.A: Avoiding all outdoor activities
options.B: Wearing heavy lead aprons
options.C: Taking daily multivitamins
options.D: Regular hand hygiene

explanation: Handwashing and hand sanitizing remove transient microorganisms, drastically reducing the transmission of infectious agents. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which agency is responsible for regulating food and dietary supplements in Nigeria?

question: Which tool do nurses use to hold and guide a suture needle securely through the skin?

question: A patient returns three days after an abortion with fever, lower tummy pain, and a bad-smelling discharge. What does this point to?

options.A: Complete abortion

question: What is the primary characteristic of individuals who are placed in quarantine?

question: Which of these is a common local carbohydrate staple you will see in Nigerian menu planning?

options.A: Olive oil
options.B: Garri

question: If a needle absolutely must be recapped in an emergency, what is the safest way to do it?

options.C: The one-handed scoop technique

question: Why is finding immunization defaulters so important for a community?

explanation: When children miss their shots, community immunity drops, making it easy for deadly infections to spread quickly among vulnerable infants. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h1)

question: What is the main difference between quarantine and isolation?

options.A: Quarantine restricts people who were exposed but are not yet sick, while isolation separates those who are already confirmed sick.
options.B: Quarantine involves giving preventive medications, while isolation involves performing major surgical procedures.
options.C: Quarantine is only used for waterborne diseases, whereas isolation is reserved exclusively for vector-borne illnesses.
options.D: Quarantine takes place in private homes, while isolation can only happen in national research laboratories.

explanation: Easy way to remember: Isolation is for those who are already sick, while quarantine is for those who were exposed and are waiting to see if they fall ill.

question: Why do community rumors about birth control often spread faster than clinical facts?

options.A: Doctors teach these rumors during nursing school
options.B: They travel easily through trusted word-of-mouth networks
options.C: The government pays people to broadcast them on radio
options.D: They are printed inside official hospital textbooks

explanation: Spot on! People naturally trust informal chats with neighbors and friends, which is why unverified stories spread so quickly.

question: What is the absolute go-to, life-saving medication for a patient experiencing dangerous anaphylaxis?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Albuterol
options.C: Diphenhydramine
options.D: Hydrocortisone

explanation: Correct! Epinephrine acts fast to open closed airways and shoot blood pressure back up when seconds count in a severe allergic emergency.

question: Which tool is best for collecting a clean soil sample for microbial isolation?

options.A: A bare human hand pressed directly onto top dirt
options.B: An unsterilized wooden stick from the ground
options.C: A sterile trowel from a few centimeters below the surface
options.D: A household sponge soaked in soapy water

explanation: Well done! Digging slightly under the topsoil with a sterile tool helps you avoid dried-out dirt and outside germs.

question: What is the primary clinical complication caused by the poliovirus?

options.A: Irreversible muscle paralysis in the limbs
options.B: High fever accompanied by a widespread skin rash
options.C: Uncontrollable fits of violent coughing
options.D: Severe chronic diarrhea and rapid dehydration

explanation: Poliovirus attacks the nervous system, which can lead to total, permanent paralysis, most commonly affecting the legs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h4)

question: What is a classic sign of left-sided neglect after a right-hemisphere stroke?

options.A: Complaining constantly about severe pain in the left arm
options.B: Refusing to speak complete sentences during a conversation
options.C: Exhibiting extreme caution and fear before attempting to walk
options.D: Unintentionally ignoring food, objects, and people on their left side

explanation: With left neglect, the brain literally fails to register the left side of the world. They aren't ignoring you on purpose—their brain just misses that side!

question: According to the Spaulding classification, how must you process a medical tool that goes deep inside sterile body tissues?

options.A: Simple soap washing
options.B: Sterilization
options.C: High-level disinfection
options.D: Low-level disinfection

explanation: If a tool enters sterile body tissues or blood vessels, it's a critical item and absolutely must be fully sterilized!

question: What tool do Nigerian nurses commonly use in local clinics to track a child's growth and immunization records?

options.A: Cardiovascular risk profile
options.B: Intensive care flow sheet
options.C: Surgical safety checklist
options.D: National Child Health Card

explanation: Correct! The Child Health Card has the WHO growth curves printed right on it, making it easy to track baby's weight during immunization visits.

question: What is the main health benefit of early breast milk (colostrum) for a newborn?

options.A: It gives them high dietary fiber
options.B: It stops jaundice from happening
options.C: It acts as a sleeping pill
options.D: It provides heavy antibodies and protein to protect the tummy

explanation: Colostrum is liquid gold! It is packed with protective antibodies (like IgA) that line the baby's gut to fight off early germs.

question: You need to add more water to a running steam generator. What is your very first step?

options.A: Ask the parent to hold the steam nozzle away
options.B: Pour cold water slowly while the unit is still boiling
options.C: Turn off and unplug the unit before adding water
options.D: Cover the hot metal parts with a dry towel first

explanation: Always power down and unplug first! This protects you from electrical shocks and nasty steam burns.

question: What is the big advantage of modern low-osmolality ORS compared to the older, stronger formula?

options.A: It reduces stool volume and the need for IV fluids
options.B: It provides all the daily vitamins a growing child needs
options.C: It tastes much sweeter and dissolves instantly in cold water
options.D: It cures bacterial infections without needing antibiotics

explanation: By lowering the sugar and salt slightly, the modern formula creates less osmotic pull in the gut, which means less watery stool and fewer trips to the hospital for drips!

question: How does severe scarring from past salpingitis increase the risk of an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Fibrous bands force the ovaries to release eggs directly into the peritoneal cavity
options.B: Scar tissue blocks the fertilized egg from traveling down to the uterus, causing it to implant in the tube
options.C: Adhesions destroy all hormonal production needed to support a normal pregnancy
options.D: Scars cause the uterus to shrink so much that eggs refuse to enter it

explanation: When scar tissue narrows or blocks the tube, a fertilized egg gets stuck and has to try to grow right there in the tube instead of the uterus.

question: Where do raw vegetables usually pick up dirt and bacterial spores?

options.A: From the chemical fertilizers sprayed on leaves
options.B: Directly from the soil during harvesting
options.C: Through the packaging materials used in transport
options.D: By absorbing them from the surrounding air

explanation: Correct! Because root crops and veggies grow right in the earth, contact with soil is the number one way they pick up environmental germs.

question: What is a very common and easily fixed cause of muscle spasms during pregnancy?

options.A: High protein intake
options.B: Excess water
options.C: Low fiber intake
options.D: Dehydration

explanation: Not drinking enough water can easily trigger muscle cramps and even make the uterus irritable. Always remind your mums to carry a water bottle!

question: Why are nurses well-positioned to advocate for food policy changes?

options.A: They are primarily responsible for writing national agricultural laws
options.B: They witness the direct health impacts of poor nutrition in clinical practice
options.C: They control the financial budgets of international food agencies
options.D: They manage the commercial distribution of imported grain

explanation: Nurses see malnutrition and diet-related disease daily, giving them firsthand evidence of policy needs. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h8)

question: A pregnant patient at 28 weeks complains of severe heartburn after eating. What is the best advice to give her?

options.A: Lie flat on your back immediately after meals to rest your digestion
options.B: Take strong laxatives every evening to empty your bowels completely
options.C: Eat small, frequent meals and avoid lying down right after eating
options.D: Drink large glasses of water with every meal to dilute stomach acid

explanation: Smaller meals keep the stomach from getting overloaded, and staying upright uses gravity to keep the acid where it belongs!

question: Why is it so important for the immune system to tell the difference between 'self' and 'non-self'?

options.A: It allows white blood cells to travel quickly through blood vessels
options.B: It prevents the immune system from attacking healthy body tissues
options.C: It ensures that red blood cells carry enough oxygen to organs
options.D: It helps the body absorb vital nutrients from digested food

explanation: Spotting the difference is key! When the immune system correctly recognizes 'self', it knows not to attack your own healthy cells. Mistakes here are what lead to autoimmune conditions.

question: Why are breast self-exams and nurse checks so vital in community settings with limited resources?

options.A: Mammography machines are often unavailable or too expensive
options.B: African women cannot develop lumps that mammograms can see
options.C: Government policies ban the use of X-ray machines
options.D: Self-examination completely replaces the need for surgery

explanation: Since shiny mammogram machines aren't in every clinic, teaching women self-examination and doing manual checks saves lives every day.

question: Why are standards essential for a nurse manager within the control process?

options.A: They provide a baseline measurement to evaluate actual nursing practice
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for shift handovers
options.C: They prevent patients from ever complaining about care
options.D: They dictate the exact salary scale for each department

explanation: A standard gives managers a clear, agreed-upon target to check if the care being delivered matches what is expected. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h1)

question: When you digest carbohydrates, what is the main sugar that enters your bloodstream?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Glucagon
options.C: Glycerol
options.D: Glycogen

explanation: Glucose is the star player here! It is the primary, easy-to-use sugar that our bodies and brains love to burn for quick energy.

question: Why is mixed methods inquiry so useful in complex healthcare settings?

options.A: It is the cheapest and fastest method to complete
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any statistical tests
options.C: It prevents patients from participating in interviews
options.D: It captures both measurable outcomes and human experiences

explanation: Combining hard numbers with human stories gives researchers a much fuller, richer picture of complicated health problems.

question: A mum on her second day after delivery hasn't passed stool and is scared to use the toilet. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Withhold all oral fluids and food until she passes flatus
options.B: Administer a strong stimulant enema immediately without consulting a doctor
options.C: Insist that she remains in bed until her bowel movement happens naturally
options.D: Encourage fluid intake, walking around, and check if stool softeners were ordered

explanation: Gentle movement, plenty of fluids, and stool softeners are the safest, kindest way to help her first postpartum toilet trip go smoothly!

question: What is the single most effective way to stop the spread of hospital infections?

options.A: Proper hand hygiene
options.B: Wearing sterile boots
options.C: Changing bed sheets daily
options.D: Spraying room air freshener

explanation: Frequent and thorough handwashing or alcohol rubbing removes transient microorganisms and stops them from passing between patients. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h3)

question: Which part of the inner ear turns sound vibrations into electrical signals for the brain?

options.A: Cochlea
options.B: Tympanic membrane
options.C: Malleus
options.D: Auditory canal

explanation: The cochlea is shaped like a little snail shell. It is packed with fluid and tiny hair cells that translate physical sound waves into nerve impulses.

question: What is the main goal of vocational rehabilitation in mental health CBR?

options.A: To replace traditional school education for young children
options.B: To keep clients busy so they do not talk to their family members
options.C: To help clients learn practical skills for earning income and gaining independence
options.D: To train clients to become fully licensed medical doctors and nurses

explanation: Vocational training equips individuals with trades like farming or tailoring, enabling them to earn money and feel productive in society. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h5)

question: Which method gives the most precise and exact picture of what a patient eats?

options.A: Monthly grocery receipt review
options.B: Standard 24-hour recall
options.C: Weighed food record
options.D: General food frequency list

explanation: Spot on! Weighing the food before eating and measuring any leftovers gives you the most accurate data possible.

question: What is the main goal of family planning right after delivery?

options.A: Eliminating all postpartum bleeding immediately
options.B: Ensuring the immediate return of normal menstruation
options.C: Speeding up the physical involution of the uterus
options.D: Preventing closely spaced and unplanned pregnancies

explanation: Postpartum family planning helps mothers space out their pregnancies, giving their bodies time to recover and protecting the health of both mom and baby! You've got this.

question: What is another common name for a food-borne illness?

options.A: Bowel obstruction
options.B: Nutritional deficiency
options.C: Gastric influenza
options.D: Food poisoning

explanation: You've got this! 'Food poisoning' is simply the everyday term we use when someone gets sick from eating or drinking something contaminated. Keep going!

question: In medical storage, what does the FEFO rule stand for?

options.A: First-Expired, First-Out
options.B: Fast-Entry, Fast-Output
options.C: Forward-Examination, Final-Order
options.D: First-Evaluated, Freight-Out

explanation: You nailed it! FEFO means items closest to their expiry date get used first so nothing goes to waste.

question: Why are lysosomes important for cellular health?

options.A: They generate chemical energy for membrane transport
options.B: They package proteins for export out of the cell
options.C: They break down waste and foreign material using enzymes
options.D: They store the genetic code for future cell divisions

explanation: Lysosomes act as the cleanup crew of the cell by using powerful digestive enzymes to destroy debris, damaged parts, and harmful invaders. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h3)

question: When is total parenteral nutrition (feeding directly into the veins) specifically needed?

options.A: When the gastrointestinal tract is completely non-functional or obstructed
options.B: When the patient simply dislikes the taste of hospital food
options.C: When the patient is able to swallow clear liquids
options.D: When the surgery only involved a minor skin biopsy

explanation: Spot on! We only use IV nutrition when the gut cannot work or is blocked, since it bypasses the digestive system completely.

question: What is the very first thing that happens during the initiation phase of cancer development?

options.A: The immune system completely destroys the mutated cell
options.B: New blood vessels sprout to feed the growing tumor mass
options.C: Abnormal cells spread through blood to distant organs
options.D: Permanent damage or mutation happens to the cell DNA

explanation: Initiation is the starting spark—it's that first permanent hit or change to the cell's DNA caused by a carcinogen.

question: What does it mean for a nursing research project to show 'originality'?

options.A: Adding fresh insights or applying concepts in a new setting
options.B: Inventing a brand-new hospital building design
options.C: Writing a research paper without using any past references
options.D: Copying successful studies from foreign countries word-for-word

explanation: Well done! Originality means bringing a fresh perspective, new data, or trying an existing idea in a brand-new setting like our local Nigerian hospitals.

question: What body regulates the Nurse Practice Act and professional standards for nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Nigerian Medical and Dental Association
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.C: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.D: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria is the statutory body charged with regulating nursing education and practice in the country. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T5#GNS324_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the biggest benefit of bringing mental health care directly into local communities?

options.A: It reduces stigma and improves accessibility to care
options.B: It eliminates the need for any trained medical professionals
options.C: It allows government agencies to stop funding hospitals
options.D: It guarantees that patients will never experience a relapse

explanation: Bringing care closer to home makes it easier for people to get help without feeling the heavy shame or fear attached to traveling to a distant psychiatric hospital.

question: How do patriarchal community structures contribute to forced marriage?

options.A: By legally requiring women to register businesses in their husband's name
options.B: By forcing young men to marry older women for inheritance
options.C: By banning all forms of traditional marriage ceremonies entirely
options.D: By giving male family members total control over female relatives' lives

explanation: Patriarchal norms concentrate decision-making power in the hands of men, making it easier to override a woman's personal choice. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h2)

question: How should active physical health records be stored when clinic hours are over?

options.A: Left open on top of desks for easy morning access
options.B: Handed out to patients to take home for safe storage
options.C: Stacked neatly on the open veranda floor
options.D: In locked cabinets to maintain security and confidentiality

explanation: Correct! Keeping files in locked cabinets protects patient privacy and prevents sensitive health information from getting lost or seen by unauthorized persons.

question: Why do doctors often prescribe hormonal contraceptives for women with oligomenorrhoea?

options.A: To induce regular withdrawal bleeding and protect the uterine lining
options.B: To permanently stop the natural production of all body hormones
options.C: To permanently cure the underlying genetic defect in the ovaries
options.D: To stimulate the immediate release of multiple eggs every month

explanation: Spot on! Contraceptives help shed the uterine lining on a regular schedule, preventing it from building up too much when natural ovulation isn't happening.

question: During heavy rainfall, animal waste and fertilizers wash off a massive grazing field into a nearby river. What type of pollution source is this?

options.A: Non-point source pollution
options.B: Municipal borehole contamination
options.C: Point source pollution
options.D: Direct industrial discharge

explanation: Because runoff comes from a broad, scattered land area rather than a single pipe, it is a non-point source. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h3)

question: When inserting a rectal suppository, past which structure must it go to stay in place?

options.A: Internal anal sphincter
options.B: The sigmoid colon
options.C: The external skin folds
options.D: The ileocecal valve

explanation: You want to push it just past that internal sphincter muscle. If you don't, the body's natural reflex will push it right back out. Good nursing touch makes all the difference!

question: What is the correct needle insertion angle for an intradermal injection?

options.A: 5 to 15 degrees
options.B: 60 to 75 degrees
options.C: 90 degrees
options.D: 45 degrees

explanation: A very shallow angle of 5 to 15 degrees keeps the needle in the superficial dermal layer instead of slipping deeper. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why is telling a worried patient 'everything will be fine' considered a poor communication habit?

options.A: It forces the patient to take extra medication
options.B: It dismisses the patient's genuine emotional distress
options.C: It violates hospital administrative laws
options.D: It lowers the patient's blood pressure too quickly

explanation: Offering false reassurance shuts down conversation. It brushes off their real fears instead of letting them safely express what's bothering them.

question: How does social media help spread harmful diet trends?

options.A: It forces government agencies to approve new superfoods daily.
options.B: It lowers the market cost of rare and exotic dietary supplements.
options.C: It creates virtual communities that make strict rules feel rewarding.
options.D: It provides rigorous peer-reviewed data from medical doctors.

explanation: Online groups make people feel like they belong to a special team when they follow harsh diet rules together. Keep up the great study flow!

question: What is the difference between monitoring and evaluation in community health programs?

options.A: Monitoring deals only with finance, while evaluation deals only with drugs
options.B: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.C: Monitoring is ongoing during the project, while evaluation assesses final outcomes
options.D: Monitoring happens after the project closes, while evaluation happens before

explanation: Monitoring happens continuously as activities are implemented, whereas evaluation measures the ultimate success or impact of the project at the end. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h7)

question: What is the main goal of giving birth control counseling during Post-Abortion Care (PAC)?

options.A: To prevent repeat unintended pregnancies and subsequent unsafe abortions
options.B: To enforce government population control quotas in rural areas
options.C: To punish the patient for engaging in premarital sex
options.D: To permanently sterilize high-risk young women

explanation: PAC counseling is all about empowering women with choices so they can protect their health and avoid future unplanned pregnancies.

question: An examiner is preparing to look at a patient's left eye using a direct ophthalmoscope. Which setup is correct?

options.A: Stand directly behind the patient and use both eyes at once
options.B: Rest the scope firmly against the bridge of the patient's nose
options.C: Hold the scope in the left hand and use the left eye
options.D: Hold the scope in the right hand and use the left eye

explanation: Using matching sides (left hand and left eye for the patient's left eye) allows the examiner to get close without colliding with the patient. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h6)

question: What special type of room ventilation is a must-have for patients on airborne precautions?

options.A: Positive pressure room
options.B: Standard natural ventilation room
options.C: Negative pressure room
options.D: Reverse isolation airflow room

explanation: Spot on! Negative pressure rooms act like a trap—when the door opens, air rushes in instead of letting infectious germs float out into the hospital hallway.

question: Which finding is most commonly auscultated in the lungs of a patient experiencing fluid overload?

options.A: High-pitched whistling wheezes
options.B: Absent breath sounds on the left
options.C: A loud friction rub over the trachea
options.D: Fine crackles at the lung bases

explanation: Fluid backing up into the tiny air sacs of the lungs creates a crackling sound when air pops them open during inhalation. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T3#GNS311_U2_T3_h5)

question: What does 'informed consent' mean when planning a home delivery?

options.A: The doctor signs a paper without telling the mother anything
options.B: The family understands the risks and benefits and agrees voluntarily
options.C: The government forces every woman to give birth at home
options.D: The traditional birth attendant makes all decisions for the family

explanation: Informed consent requires that patients are fully aware of what they are choosing and agree of their own free will. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h8)

question: Why is it so important to keep raw meat away from foods you are ready to eat?

options.A: To prevent cross-contamination of harmful bacteria
options.B: To improve the overall taste of cooked dishes
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of meal storage
options.D: To speed up the cooking process on the stove

explanation: Keeping raw items separate stops germs from jumping onto food items that won't be cooked again before eating.

question: Why is good room ventilation a must in spaces where chemical disinfectants like glutaraldehyde are used?

options.A: To prevent toxic vapors from accumulating and harming respiratory tracts
options.B: To cool down high-speed mechanical washer-disinfector units
options.C: To speed up the drying time of washed stainless steel basins
options.D: To reduce ambient room humidity so metal instruments do not rust

explanation: These strong chemicals give off fumes that can mess with your lungs if they build up in a closed, stuffy room. Always keep the air moving!

question: Which type of dietary fiber is especially important to include in the daily meals of older adults?

options.A: Low-residue fiber to completely eliminate bowel movements
options.B: Synthetic fiber powders to speed up stomach emptying
options.C: Animal-derived fiber to build stronger intestinal walls
options.D: High-fiber foods to prevent chronic constipation

explanation: Well done! Because bowel movements tend to slow down with age, fiber is a simple superhero for adding bulk and preventing painful constipation.

question: Why should a nurse manager mix and match different motivational theories on the ward?

options.A: Different nurses have unique professional needs and career drivers
options.B: Only one theory applies to nurses working night shifts
options.C: Using a single theory is illegal under labor laws
options.D: Hospital accreditation boards require all theories to be used equally

explanation: Spot on! Every nurse is different. What motivates a fresh graduate might be totally different from what drives a senior nursing officer.

question: How do nurses accurately measure fluid output from a heavy surgical dressing or pad?

options.A: Estimating the stain size using a common ruler
options.B: Squeezing the fluid out into a measuring cup
options.C: Asking the patient how much fluid they think leaked
options.D: Weighing the wet item and subtracting the dry weight

explanation: Weight is the most reliable way to quantify fluid soaked into solid materials, where one gram roughly equals one milliliter. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h5)

question: What is a major danger of giving high-flow oxygen to a patient who retains carbon dioxide?

options.A: Rapid increase in the patient's daily fluid retention
options.B: Loss of the hypoxic drive, leading to respiratory depression
options.C: Sudden development of severe skin allergies on the face
options.D: Permanent discoloration of the nose and cheek tissues

explanation: Some chronic lung patients breathe because their oxygen is low. Giving too much oxygen can make their brain say 'we don't need to breathe anymore,' which is dangerous.

question: Which of the following is a suitable health topic for discussion at a PTA meeting?

options.A: Malaria prevention and insecticide-treated nets
options.B: Commercial transport licensing procedures
options.C: How to write university entrance examinations
options.D: The stock market price of agricultural goods

explanation: Malaria prevention is a critical public health topic that directly affects school attendance and student well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h4)

question: A nurse writes in an incident report: 'The lazy night shift nurse forgot the antibiotic.' Why is this wrong?

options.A: It does not state the financial cost of the missed dose
options.B: It fails to mention the exact name of the drug
options.C: It includes confidential medical diagnosis codes
options.D: It uses judgmental language instead of objective facts

explanation: Spot on. Calling a colleague 'lazy' is an opinion, not a fact. Stick to what was observed, like the exact time the medication was missed.

question: Which of these is NOT a normal job of a healthy kidney?

options.A: Filtering and breaking down peptide hormones
options.B: Making large amounts of dietary insulin
options.C: Releasing erythropoietin when oxygen is low
options.D: Clearing parathyroid hormone from the blood

question: Why should a 38-year-old client who gets migraines with aura avoid combined oral contraceptives?

options.A: It triggers severe allergic skin rashes on the face
options.B: It will cause her migraines to happen every single day
options.C: It significantly increases her risk of having a stroke
options.D: It stops the migraine medication from working properly

explanation: This is a classic safety rule in pharmacology: migraines with aura, plus estrogen, plus being over 35 multiplies the risk of a dangerous stroke.

question: What type of cartilage stays on the ends of bones inside your movable joints throughout life?

options.A: Elastic cartilage
options.B: Fibrocartilage pad
options.C: Epiphyseal cartilage
options.D: Articular cartilage

explanation: Articular cartilage acts like a smooth cushion on the ends of your bones so they can glide past each other smoothly in your joints.

question: What happens when hospital administrators treat MBO as just a bureaucratic checklist?

options.A: Patient satisfaction increases across all departments
options.B: The hospital saves money on administrative salaries
options.C: Staff quickly lose interest and trust in the process
options.D: Nurses become expert planners overnight

question: Which health condition is often managed with a low-calorie diet?

options.A: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.B: Advanced neurodegenerative palsy
options.C: Acute iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Chronic primary insomnia

question: A nurse agrees to perform a 'mild' form of FGM in a private clinic to save a young girl from a harsher traditional cut. What could happen to this nurse?

options.A: A minor warning from the local hospital management board

question: Which of these is a great example of a non-verbal communication cue during a patient interaction?

options.A: Body posture and facial expressions
options.B: Medical jargon used in charting
options.C: The specific tone of spoken words
options.D: A written discharge instruction

question: What makes primary health care nurses so crucial for disease surveillance?

options.A: They are responsible for funding national health budgets.

options.C: They write the international guidelines for disease control.
options.D: They interact directly with patients daily and spot early signs of disease.

explanation: As frontline nurses, you are the eyes and ears of health surveillance because you see the patients first every single day!

question: Why do dietitians recommend high-fiber complex carbs instead of simple sugars for diabetic patients?

options.A: They stimulate the pancreas to grow new beta cells
options.B: They contain zero calories and cannot be converted into fat
options.C: They slow down digestion and prevent rapid blood sugar spikes
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for any diabetes medication

question: Where do home health care services mainly take place?

options.A: Inside specialized palliative care centers
options.B: Inside the private residences of patients
options.C: Inside crowded tertiary hospital wards
options.D: Inside government-run primary health clinics

question: Which task can a registered nurse safely delegate to a nursing assistant?

options.A: Measuring routine vital signs on a stable patient
options.B: Performing a clinical assessment on a deteriorating patient
options.C: Administering a complex intravenous chemotherapy drug
options.D: Formulating the initial nursing care plan on admission
